reflections.title: "Worshiped the Lord but Also Served Their Idols"

reflect.text: When the king of Assyria moved foreigners into Samaria, lions attacked the settlers. The people assumed the Lord was merely a local god who needed to be appeased so the trouble would stop. Even after an exiled priest arrived to teach them God's ways, they simply added the Lord to their collection of idols. Instead of giving Him their true devotion, they mixed worship of the Lord with their old customs. This blended religion persisted for generations, passing empty traditions down to their children.

We can easily slip into the same pattern today. We might attend church and carry out outward rituals simply to look good or ease our fears, while our hearts remain far from God. As F. B. Meyer warned, "God will never be in competition with another." When we try to divide our lives between the Lord and other pursuits, whatever competes with Him actually holds our heart. God does not accept half-hearted service, but calls for our exclusive trust and sincere worship.

questions: What worldly desires or habits compete with God for first place in your daily life?
How can you move from merely outward religious routines to sincere, undivided devotion to the Lord?
reflections.prayer: Lord, forgive us for the times we offer You outward worship while giving our hearts to other things. Help us to put away every idol and serve You with undivided loyalty. Teach us to trust You alone as our only Master every day of the week. Amen.
